title: CoffeeCo – what drives daily store revenue?
text: You are the marketing manager of CoffeeCo, a chain of coffee shops, and want to forecast daily revenue per store (in €) from one year of store-day data.

Independent variables: temperature (°C), promo (promotion day: no = 0, yes = 1), price (price of a latte in €), weekend (Mon–Fri = 0, Sat/Sun = 1), app_users (loyalty-app users living near the store, in hundreds).
Revenue = β0 + β1·temperature + β2·promo + β3·price + β4·weekend + β5·app_users. The overall model has an R² of 58% and is statistically significant.

title: Value-in-use: LED spotlights for a hotel
text: A hotel uses 600 halogen spotlights. It pays 4 € per halogen lamp, and each lamp lasts 6 months.
A supplier offers an LED spotlight that lasts 2 years. Over a year, a halogen lamp consumes electricity worth 20 €, an LED lamp electricity worth 5 €.
Every replacement of a lamp (halogen or LED) causes 2 € of labour cost for the maintenance team.

title: Trend report extract: "The Rest Economy"
text: Rest is the new status symbol. After years of always-on work and blurred boundaries between office and home since the pandemic, burned-out professionals are investing in sleep like never before. Smart rings and watches now measure sleep quality every night, and their scores are proudly shared with friends.

City dwellers in ever-denser, noisier metropolitan areas book "sleep retreats": hotels offer sleep concierges, soundproof rooms and pillow menus. Mattress brands sell subscriptions that adapt firmness to your data.
Consumers increasingly expect the brands around them – from hotels to employers – to actively protect and improve their rest, and to prove it with data.
Source: fictitious trend report written for practice.

title: Mini case FitHub – a premium membership for a gym chain
text: FitHub runs 40 gyms. With rising demand for guided training, it plans a new premium membership. Its true competitive advantages are its certified personal coaches and its training app. FitHub separates its members into four strategic segments.
Monthly margin = 60% of the monthly fee (the rest covers operating costs). Retention rates are monthly.
To decide on the product, FitHub ran a rating-based conjoint analysis (1–10 scale) with representative members of each segment.
